name: Malta
tagline: The EU country where the whole university already runs in English
summary: Malta is the odd one out in the EU: English is an official language and the University of Malta states plainly that 'the language of instruction and communication at UM is English'. That means you get an EU degree, EU freedom of movement and no visa, without the language problem you hit in Slovenia or Greece. Better still, Malta treats the IB Diploma as a local qualification rather than a foreign one, and publishes exactly how IB grades map onto the Maltese Matriculation Certificate.
whyConsider: English is an official language and all University of Malta teaching is in English - no language barrier and no language test to game
The IB is treated as a local qualification, with a published conversion: HL counts as Advanced Level, SL as Intermediate Level
The entry bar is clear and reasonable: the IB Diploma with at least 28 points, with passes at 3 or better in a language, a science and a humanistic subject
You are an EU citizen, so no visa, no health surcharge and free public transport once you hold an e-residence permit
One small campus at Msida where almost everything happens, which makes settling in easier than a big city university
watchOuts: Accommodation is the real cost: UM's own estimate is EUR 550-700 a month for a shared room and EUR 800-1,600 for a single
Undergraduate tuition is published course by course rather than as one table, so you have to look it up per course in the online course search
Malta is small - around 500,000 people - and the subject range is narrower than a large mainland university

Application deadlines for the October 2027 intake were not published as of 23 September 2026. In the 2026 cycle the main deadline was 22 July at 14:00 - after IB results, which is unusual and good - but medicine closed on 16 March at 14:00 for IB holders, four months before results.
Subjects at IB ab initio level 'are not comparable to any subjects required for admission' - check your subject choices against the course requirements early
Every University of Malta deadline falls at 14:00 Malta time, not at midnight, and the late-application safety net does not apply to medicine or to any course with a limited number of places.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: The International Baccalaureate Diploma with at least 28 points, with passes at 3 points or better in a language, a science and a humanistic subject.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: The University of Malta states: 'Higher Level (HL) subjects are normally accepted where a MATSEC Advanced Level is required, while Standard Level (SL) subjects are normally accepted where a MATSEC Intermediate Level is required.' It also states that 'Subjects at Ab Initio are not comparable to any subjects required for admission.'
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: IB grade 7 = MATSEC Grade A; 6 = B; 5 = C; 4 = D; 3 = E, which is the minimum pass.
notes: Malta classes the International Baccalaureate as a LOCAL qualification, not an overseas one. When you apply you select 'Local Qualifications', not 'Overseas Qualifications' - getting this wrong will misroute your application.

The Maltese Matriculation Certificate that IB is compared against consists of six subjects: two at Advanced Level, three at Intermediate Level, plus Systems of Knowledge. The general entry requirement also includes a pass at grade 5 or better in English, Maltese and Mathematics at SEC level; how that Maltese requirement is applied to an IB applicant was not stated on the pages read and should be confirmed with Admissions.
How Theory of Knowledge is treated against the Maltese Systems of Knowledge requirement was not stated on the pages read on 2026-09-22.
Individual courses set their own subject requirements on top of the general one - check the course page.

deadlines.label: University of Malta - main application deadline
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadlines were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.notes: Precedent, read on 23 September 2026: "Applications for all courses are to be submitted online against the relevant application fee up to 22 July 2026 at 14:00." Note the time: 14:00 Malta time, not midnight. This is one of the very few main deadlines in Europe that falls after IB results are released, which is the single best reason for an IB student to look at Malta. The application fee is non-refundable, and the previous record here gave no main deadline at all - it said only that "the main deadline falls earlier" than the late one.

deadlines.label: Doctor of Medicine and Surgery - the deadline for applicants presenting an IB Diploma
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadlines were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.audience: applicants to the M.D. presenting an IB Diploma, a European Baccalaureate or the MATSEC Matriculation Certificate
deadlines.notes: Promoted to its own entry on 23 September 2026. It was in no record, it names the IB explicitly, and it is more than four months earlier than the main deadline. Precedent, read on 23 September 2026: "Applicants presenting qualifications considered local (e.g., IB, EB, or the Matriculation Certificate awarded by MATSEC) ... were required to submit their application by 16 March 2026 at 14:00." The useful half of this is that Malta counts an IB Diploma as a local qualification rather than an overseas one, which buys you six extra weeks over the overseas-qualification deadline. The dangerous half is that March is four months before your results, and the University does not accept late applications for the M.D. at all.

deadlines.label: Doctor of Medicine and Surgery - the earlier deadline for overseas qualifications
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadlines were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.audience: applicants to the M.D. presenting qualifications other than the IB, the EB or a MATSEC certificate
deadlines.notes: Precedent, read on 23 September 2026: "The closing date for receipt of applications from applicants presenting overseas qualifications and degrees awarded by institutions other than the University of Malta was 30 January 2026 at 14:00." Recorded here so that the IB deadline above is visible as the concession it is: if you are taking A-levels or a national diploma rather than the IB, you are applying to Maltese medicine in January.

deadlines.label: Faculty of Health Sciences, limited-number courses - last chance to change your order of preference
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadline was not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.audience: applicants who chose a Faculty of Health Sciences course with a limited number of places
deadlines.notes: Promoted to its own entry on 23 September 2026. It is the least visible date in the Maltese cycle and it decides which course you are actually offered. The University publishes it as: applicants selecting limited-enrolment programmes offered by the Faculty of Health Sciences may adjust their order of preference "only until 31 August at 14:00". After that the order you last saved is the order you are placed against. The wording carries no year, which is why no year is inferred here.

deadlines.label: Late application deadline - and the courses it does not rescue
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadlines were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.notes: Precedent, read on 23 September 2026: "Late applications may be submitted up to 15 September 2026 at 14:00, where late application fees will be charged." The part that matters more than the date: late applications are not accepted for the M.D. course, nor for any course with a limited number of students. So the safety net exists for ordinary degrees and does not exist for exactly the courses people miss deadlines for.

deadlines.label: Deadline for non-EU applicants who need a visa
deadlines.year: October 2027 intake - the 2027 deadlines were not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.audience: applicants who are not EU citizens and need a visa to travel to Malta
deadlines.notes: Precedent, read on 23 September 2026: "The deadline for Non-EU applicants submitting an application towards courses commencing in October 2026, and requiring a visa to travel to Malta, is 1 July 2026 at 14:00." Applications received after it are deferred to the next intake rather than refused. As a Danish or other EU citizen you are not bound by this earlier date and the July main deadline is yours.

deadlines.label: University of Malta - main application window opens
deadlines.year: Annual pattern; the October 2027 opening date was not published on 2026-09-23
deadlines.notes: Recorded in an earlier pass as "Applications open from the November before the October start". That wording could not be found again on the dates-and-deadlines page on 23 September 2026, which by then showed only that the October 2026 cycle had closed, so it is left here as an unverified description of the annual pattern rather than as a date. The University of Malta runs a main intake every October and a smaller one in February. Treat the opening as some time in the preceding winter and take the real date from um.edu.mt once the 2027 cycle is posted.

deadlines.label: University of Malta - first semester begins for first-year students
deadlines.notes: Published on the University’s academic calendar and read on 23 September 2026: "Monday 4 October 2027 to Saturday 5 February 2028 - For first year students", with continuing students starting a week earlier on 27 September 2027 and the opening ceremony on 4 October. The previous record here said the 2027-28 calendar was not published; it is, in full. First-semester examinations run 17 January to 5 February 2028, the second semester runs 7 February to 28 June 2028, and there is a September assessment period from 1 to 15 September 2028.

steps: Find your course in the UM online course finder at um.edu.mt/courses and read its specific entry requirements and its fee, which is shown on the course's own fees tab.
Check your IB subjects against the requirement: HL counts as Advanced Level, SL as Intermediate Level, and ab initio subjects do not count at all.
Apply online through the UM application system, selecting 'Local Qualifications' because Malta treats the IB as local.
Satisfy the English language requirement. Applicants educated outside Malta normally present a Secure English Language Test result; some are exempt, and UM runs its own ISET test on campus.

Submit before the published deadline for your intake and have your original documents verified. In the 2026 cycle that meant 22 July at 14:00 for most courses, 16 March at 14:00 for the M.D., and 31 August at 14:00 as the last day to reorder your preferences for a limited-number Health Sciences course.
As an EU citizen, move to Malta and apply to Identita for an eResidence card, which also gets you free public transport.
application.selectionNotes: Some courses admit a fixed number of students. The University confirms this indirectly and in the place it matters: it does not accept late applications "for the M.D. course or courses with limited student numbers", and it lets applicants for limited-enrolment Faculty of Health Sciences programmes adjust their order of preference "only until 31 August at 14:00", which is how a ranked allocation behaves. The exact capped list and the numbers were not published on any page read on 2026-09-22 or 2026-09-23 - check the individual course page. Application fees are non-refundable, and late applications carry an additional fee.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: All of them. The University of Malta states that 'the language of instruction and communication at UM is English'. Maltese is the other official language of the country but is not needed for study.
language.englishProof: Applicants educated outside Malta must normally present a Secure English Language Test (SELT). UM accepts TOEFL iBT (80 for undergraduate), Academic IELTS (up to 6.5 depending on level; 5.5 for Foundation Studies), Cambridge Advanced Certificate, Pearson PTE Academic (59-71 by level), Trinity College London ISE, and its own on-campus ISET test (bands 4-6 by level). Whether IB English A or B counts as an exemption was not stated on the pages read - ask Admissions, since the FAQs note that even fluent English speakers are not exempted from presenting documentation.
notes: Malta is genuinely bilingual in everyday life: Maltese and English are both official, and you can live there entirely in English.
The general entry requirement refers to a SEC pass in Maltese as well as English and Mathematics; confirm with Admissions how that is applied to an IB applicant who has never studied Maltese.

livingCostMonthly.value: UM's own estimate: shared accommodation EUR 550-700; single accommodation EUR 800-1,600; food and drink EUR 450 (excluding eating out); mobile and wi-fi EUR 30; laundry EUR 80-100; electricity and water EUR 50 at the basic rate; other expenses EUR 200-300. Public transport is free for e-residence permit holders. That gives a total of roughly EUR 1,360-2,530 a month depending on whether you share.
livingCostMonthly.year: Undated on the page read on 2026-09-22; UM describes the figures as 'a more realistic figure for the cost of living at the moment'

notes: UM does not publish one undergraduate fee table. It states that 'The tuition/enrolment fees are available through the fees tab while searching for a course through the online search facility', so you must look up your specific course. This is the single biggest gap in this file and needs filling per course.

As a reference point for the scale of the EU/non-EU gap at UM, its published doctoral fees are EUR 600 a year full-time for EU/EEA students versus EUR 11,000 a year for non-EU students. Do not assume undergraduate fees follow the same ratio - check the course page.
UK nationals have been treated as non-EU nationals for UM fee purposes since January 2021.
Accommodation, not tuition, is what makes Malta expensive.

funding: UM lists scholarships for Tunisian nationals, for Palestinian nationals, and ISSI postgraduate scholarships. No scholarship aimed at EU undergraduate applicants was found on the pages read.
UM references stipends and the 'Get Qualified' scheme, but the pages read described these as being for local students.
Danish SU for a full degree abroad requires programme approval by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen - check with your studievejleder.
residency: As a Danish or other EU citizen you have the right to live and study in Malta. You apply to Identita for an eResidence card, which UM covers on its 'Visa and e-residence permit' pages. Holding the e-residence permit also gives you free public transport. Non-EU students need a student visa and must apply much earlier - the previous cycle's visa-applicant deadline was 1 July, three and a half months before the October start.
housing: This is the thing to plan first. UM's own estimate is EUR 550-700 a month for shared accommodation and EUR 800-1,600 for a single place, so sharing is close to compulsory on a student budget. The UM International Office assists with accommodation; start looking as soon as you accept an offer.
healthcare: As an EU citizen bring your EU health insurance card for necessary care in the Maltese public system. UM's International Office covers health and support services for students; detailed requirements for non-EU students were not published on the pages read on 2026-09-22.

institutions.name: University of Malta
institutions.englishBachelors: All undergraduate courses are taught in English, across faculties from Arts and Science to Medicine, Law, Engineering and ICT
institutions.note: The national university and effectively the only full university in the country - it publishes a clear, generous IB conversion and teaches everything in English.

institutions.name: Malta College of Arts, Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Vocational and applied bachelor degrees taught in English; a count was not verified on the pages read
institutions.note: Malta's vocational college, offering applied bachelor degrees with a stronger practical and placement element than UM.

institutions.name: Institute of Tourism Studies
institutions.englishBachelors: Tourism, hospitality and culinary bachelor degrees taught in English; a count was not verified
institutions.note: The specialist tourism and hospitality school, on a purpose-built campus at Smart City outside Valletta.

institutions.name: American University of Malta
institutions.englishBachelors: American-style bachelor degrees taught in English; a count was not verified
institutions.note: A small private American-model university in the Three Cities; verify its current programme list and accreditation directly before applying.

institutions.name: Middlesex University Malta
institutions.englishBachelors: UK-awarded bachelor degrees taught in English; a count was not verified
institutions.note: A branch campus of a London university, so you get a UK degree while living in the EU - useful if you wanted a British degree without the British fees and visa.

institutions.name: St Martin's Institute of Higher Education
institutions.englishBachelors: University of London degrees delivered in English; a count was not verified
institutions.note: Delivers University of London programmes in Malta; small, and worth checking directly since its offering is tied to an external awarding body.

institutions.name: Global College Malta
institutions.englishBachelors: Taught in English; programme list and current status were not verified on the pages read
institutions.note: A small private college - confirm it is still operating and still accredited by MFHEA before applying.
